summary: Established a robust architectural governance framework utilizing AST-based parsing, transactional indexing, and information-theoretic telemetry (KL divergence) to ensure system determinism. Further refined integrity monitoring by implementing a Bayesian Beta-Binomial model to distinguish transient glitches from systemic failures, shifting progress metrics toward verifiable self-correction robustness.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and model pinning ensure system determinism, while DSR-based SRS models provide superior scalability.
Coupling index updates to atomic patch operations prevents index drift and fragmentation.
Information theory (KL divergence) and Bayesian inference provide a robust mathematical foundation for identifying systemic anomalies and tracking system health.
Architectural metrics are most effective when tracking specific, verifiable outputs and self-correction mechanisms rather than abstract progress.
